The skeleton said the mace was out of power,
but perhaps it still has enough to
destroy the back of the safe.

Judge
He's clutching a small key.

Your Honour! This is my brother Gooka.
I think he's the one who murdered our father!
That's a serious accusation.
He must have poisoned him with winter stalactites!
Is that true? Do you have winter stalactites?
Yes, I do.
What for?

I needed them for experiments. But they're safely stored away. I
keep them cold so that no poison leaches out.
That's it! Your Honour! That's how he poisoned our father!

Woman, enough of this nonsense! Your
father wasn't killed by winter stalactite poison. That's perfectly clear!
That poison leaves purple blotches on the body,
and your father's are green.

As far as I know, that's caused by a very
rare poison from distant lands called barut. I've never seen it here
in Relov. Making it requires some very unusual ingredients.
Gooka did it! I know he did!
Be quiet. So far, nothing suggests that Gooka is the murderer.
Your Honour, what ingredients are needed to make that poison?

Even I don't know exactly. Your father Mahara mentioned it once
when we were discussing rare poisons. But even he
didn't have all the substances it requires.
Will you find out who murdered Sage Mahara, Your Honour?

Of course not! That's your task. Until you can prove your innocence,
you may not leave the estate. I strongly suspect, indeed I'm almost certain,
that the murderer had an accomplice in your household.

You're probably right. My father rarely went out, and
he never ate or drank outside the house.
Show pouch
Gooka, have you learned anything new about your father's case?
Your Honour, I think my sister Baroda poisoned Father.
That's not true! He did it, and now he's trying to blame me!
I found this pouch in her room.

It's made from the hide of an Algi beast. I don't
know what's inside, and I didn't dare open it... What if...
My lover will kill me! This wasn't supposed to happen!
Your lover?

I don't know his name. He's a foreigner, and he's beautiful!
He promised to take me away from here and marry me!
I see. Albert, take her away!
So I'm no longer suspected of murder?

No, but if you want to become a Sage, you must find out why your father
was murdered. Your sister prepared the poison and gave it to him, but it
wasn't her idea. She couldn't have obtained that foreign poison alone. And
I'm sure her lover is long gone. So it's up to you, my dear Gooka.
Yes, Your Excellency.

Stop! Until Sage Mahara's murder has been solved, no
one may touch anything in this room!
I'm sorry.
My trusty, sharp dagger.
Hmm, Grandfather once brought down a mountain tuskhorn with this arrow.
note: Invented animal name: zuborozec rendered tuskhorn; no visual confirmation.

think the judge ought to see this!
I could use a key for this lock...
Force lock

Hmm, belts, ornaments, jewellery. That's Baroda all over.

Good morning, Korvana. What's for breakfast today?

A terrible thing has happened, young master. A terrible thing.
Your father is dead. The judge says you're to report to the study.
What a dreadful morning, Korvana.
Yes, young master. A tragedy. Such a tragedy...
Korvana, have you noticed anything strange lately?
What sort of strange thing?
I don't know. Something unusual. Something that doesn't normally...
Well, I don't know...
Think!

This house has been peaceful for years. Everything runs as it should. But
now that I think about it, the only new thing lately is
that your sister Baroda has taken up cooking.
What?

The afternoon before yesterday, I came into the kitchen and found your sister cooking something. She's
never done that before. She must be thinking of marriage.
My sister? C O O K I N G???

Well, she said a friend had recommended a
special spice for meat, and she wanted to try it.
And she had her own spices?
Yes, young master. She had several little bags.
Thank you. You've been a great help.
You don't happen to have a key to Baroda's room?
Yes, I clean in there, but I found it broken this morning. You can have it.
They've taken my sister away for murder.

A tragedy, such a tragedy... How
could your sister have done it?
Apparently some man put her up to it.

That might be the lanky fellow I saw
with her behind the house three evenings ago.
What lanky fellow?

In the dim light, he reminded me very much of
Sage Mahara and Master Digor when they first came to Relov.
My father wasn't Bonian?
No. Your father was much taller than anyone from around here.
I thought that was just a coincidence. Where was he from?

I don't know, but Master Digor was just as tall
and thin. You take more after your mother, who was Bonian.
And what happened to this Digor?

I'm not sure. He vanished a few weeks later. That was
when your father bought this house and began rebuilding the whole place.
Do you know where he went?

I can't say for certain. It was such a long time ago. But
I think he was heading somewhere towards the northern sea.
So you don't know anything else about him?

Not really. Although, come to think of it, a mind-emptied messenger
came from the sea once or twice over the years. He
sat in the storeroom next door while he waited for your father's reply.
note: Vymozkovany rendered mind-emptied, also used for the needle.

english: Don't tell me you didn't ask where he was from.

I did, but you know what they're like, young master.
Nothing in their heads but their task. He kept going on about
Avaral and King Heras and his adviser. Where is that?

He was talking about the Svan kingdom.
Perhaps this Digor knows something about my father's death. It looks as though
I'll have to set out on a journey.
Coal

By order of the judge, no one may leave this house.
Damn.
I can leave, but I don't know where to look beyond this house...
Thank you, Glux, my dear friend.
I was glad to help, my lord.
Here we are again.

Now we know the truth about Glux. I must go
home and tell Father everything. Perhaps he'll finally understand what
sort of man Penza is.

Meanwhile, I'll take another look around Orint Monastery. Glux
mentioned a secret library beneath the altar.
Take care of yourself.
You too.
The door is locked.
This lockpick won't open this door.
Well, this door could be unlocked!
I'd better not disturb His Belligerence just now.
They won't just let me in.

Where do you think you're going, runt?!
Excuse me?
I said, where do you think you're going?
I'm looking for the king's adviser.
As if he'd have time to talk to you.

I am Gooka, son of Sage Mahara of
Relov, and therefore a representative of the Bonian
state. I have just arrived and seek the king's adviser.

Anyone could say that. I can't let every
vagabond in. His Belligerence, King of Avaral, is
discussing plans for a new war with
his adviser. They don't wish to be disturbed.

Here are my father's credentials. If you read them,
you'll see that they also apply to me as
his heir. So kindly let me through.
All right. You may go in.
The guard wouldn't let me in.
Adviser
King

Your Belligerence, allow me to introduce myself. I am Gooka,
son and sole heir of Sage Mahara, a member
of the Bonian Council of Elders.

What brings a messenger from the distant
Bonian realm? What tidings will delight our ears?

I bring greetings from Patriarch Lekan, my superior. He
will always pray for your campaigns against the vile
Cymiks, who make life so difficult for every civilised nation.
And I hope the god Glux heeds him.

He surely will. No one worships the sea god Glux more
fervently than Patriarch Lekan. Not a day passes without his paying homage to
our god in the Temple of the Fading Dawn.

We too attend devotions at Orint Monastery. Soon we
shall offer our god Glux the greatest sacrifice
a king can make: our daughter Lidra. We
trust you will attend the ceremony as well.

Surely the kindly god Glux cannot ask us to... Of
course, I would be delighted to attend. It is a great honour.
We sail tomorrow at dawn.
Your Belligerence, I have one more humble request.
Yes?

If Your Belligerence has no objection, I need to
speak to your adviser.

Indeed? My adviser and dearest friend Penza will surely
spare you a few moments of his precious time.
Penza? But I wanted to speak to your adviser Digor.

That traitor whom Glux himself recently punished? I
would never have discovered his treachery against my
rule without Penza here, and our beloved god
Glux, who cut the treacherous Digor's life considerably short.
Is he dead?

Oh, no. While we were travelling through the Amarat
Desert, inspecting our troops together, the great Glux himself
suddenly descended upon Digor from a clear sky and struck
him with bolts of wrath.
What happened?

In his terrible anger at Digor's arrogant sins, he punished him with
a fate worse than death: he turned him into a senile,
babbling old man who must be spoon-fed.
Where is he now?

We meant to leave him on the rubbish heap, but at Princess
Lidra's request we kept him under heavy guard in his rooms.
May I see him?

I don't think that would be appropriate. If you intend to attend
the sacrifice, you should not defile yourself with such a sinner's presence.
But I...

We dismiss you with our blessing, traveller. Go now to
Orint Monastery and cleanse your soul before the coming ceremony.

Your Belligerence! Forgive me for troubling you
once more with my insignificant presence.
We expected to see you again only at the sacrifice.
While studying at Orint Monastery, I came across...
But we sent you there to contemplate, not to study. For shame!

Nevertheless, I did, Your Belligerence, though I
humbly apologise. And I found something I
should like to clarify.

In Saint Ruiciman's book, Glux: The Established
Facts, I learned that our beloved god Glux
cannot fly. It even says he
dislikes the air. So I don't understand how he
could have attacked your former adviser from above.

Heresy, Your Belligerence! Heresy of the foulest kind!
He denies the deeds of our god. With
my own eyes, I saw our almighty god
descend from the sky in terrible wrath.
Your words, dear Penza, are proof enough for us.
But it's written in Saint Ruiciman's book, and he...

I suggest you send him with your daughter Lidra as her servant.
Let Glux himself decide what to do with such a heretic.
But I...

Let it be as my wise first adviser has
said. Guards, seize him and take him to the ship.
Clearly, we can delay the sacrifice no longer. Heresy
and treason are spreading. We sail at once!
Your Belligerence. Princess.
Gooka! At last! What did you find at the monastery?
There really is a secret room beneath the altar. But there are no books there.
What is there, then?

You won't believe it, but there's an altar to Gurha the Time-Devourer.
The very creature that did such harm to Digor.
Really?

When I followed Glux's advice and opened the secret entrance, I fell
straight into a service. Their leader, apparently the high priest, immediately
ordered them to put me in chains. He said I was
under arrest for heresy.
The same accusation Penza made.

But he couldn't hold his tongue. He let slip that
their god isn't Glux, but Gurha. He also told me
Gurha lives in Parentis.
That's the abandoned city near the Western Mountains.
How could Glux's monks...
I'd say Penza has something to do with that too.
Where is he, anyway?

The moment he saw me alive and well, he went pale
and hurried off. He said he had to consult the high
priest of Orint Monastery about something urgent.

He may not have been lying about that. It seems Penza and the
high priest are allies. But not your allies, Your Belligerence.

It's all so tangled. It seems Penza isn't the
loyal friend he claimed to be, and my former
adviser Digor was wrongly accused.
So you believe us now?

I no longer know what to believe. I certainly trust you
more than Penza now. If only I could speak to Digor...
I never liked him much. He could be very disagreeable when
something displeased him, but...

Glux gave me a seed from the plant of youth. He says
the juice of its fruit should help Digor. May I have your permission?
Very well. Try it.
But how will you get the fruit when all you have is a seed?
I'll think of something. Where can I find Digor?

In the rear wing of the palace. We've unlocked the door now, after
trying to speak to him. But he's in a very bad way.
All right. I'd better go.
Young Master Gooka. Welcome, my friend. How did things go in Relov?
Yes, you were right. I found the shem.

Things are very bad here. Penza and the high priest
have won over part of the army and declared my father
a heretic who defies the will of Glux.

A heretic again? They really ought to think of
something more original.

They've fortified Zweral. Fortunately, enough troops stayed loyal
to us that we can hold them in check
for now. Unless Gurham comes to their aid. We
couldn't withstand Marin-Danim power for long.
What do you intend to do?

Our best hope is to be rid of Gurham once and for
all. I've thought about it at length. Gooka, you're truly
your father's son, and you've done very well so
far. Would you undertake an extremely dangerous expedition?

I don't know. All I originally had to do was discover who killed
my father and why. Now I know. On the other hand, after
all this, I can't just walk away. What did you have in mind?

It may sound mad. You would have to enter
the Forbidden Mountains and penetrate the Marin-Danim Fortress itself.
Once inside, try to find the missing shem and take
Gurham's from him somehow. Then find the ship's central
control panel and blow the whole nest sky-high.

That really is a mad plan. I doubt I could survive
it.
Yes, that's true.

But if we destroy the Fortress, we'll destroy all
the inventions the Marin-Danim possess.

That's true too. But almost all that's left there are
weapons, and the risk of their misuse is enormous. If only
your father and I had realised it when we could still do
something.
Wouldn't it be better if you did it yourself?

I'm not trying to shirk my responsibility, but I must stay
here. Without my help, Avaral would fall.

That's right, Gooka. Without Digor, I would be dead and
Avaral in ruins. If only I'd realised it sooner.

You're the only person who can succeed, Gooka, and the only one
we can trust.
In that case... How do I get to the Fortress?

Excellent. The Fortress lies in the heart of the Forbidden Mountains.
You can reach it through Alkan Pass. Be careful:
Gurham has put sinchas there. You surely know how dangerous those
toothed crustaceans are.
I've heard about them.

I think you'll see the Fortress in the distance just beyond the
pass. In my day, we used a teleporter to get inside. That
may have changed. After that, you're on your own.
Can't you give me any more advice?

I haven't been there for nearly half a century, so everything has
probably changed. In my day, a lift linked the spaceship
to the Fortress. I believe you could also get in through
the sewer shafts. But as I said, things may be different
now.
Is that everything?

I can't think of anything else. Above all, remember that you have the shems
and the controller. They may come in useful.
And here are the gloves you wanted.
Gloves made of Algi hide? A wise decision.

Very well. Goodbye, Lidra. Goodbye, Digor. Goodbye, Your
Belligerence. All I can do is try.
Take care of yourself. You must come back. I love you.
May Glux's will guide you!
Remember: the fate of all Janatris now rests on you alone!

english: Hooha mmmm... Kuhkha.
Here, take this.
Where am I? What's happening? Run, all of you! Gurha!!!

Calm down. There's no danger now. You're in
Avaral, in your own rooms.

Phew, I was lucky. When Gurha attacked me, I
thought I was finished. You can't imagine the
torment his anti-stasis field causes. You feel your body ageing
and your mind slowly dying. After that, I remember
nothing. Who are you, anyway?
I'm Gooka, son of Sage Mahara.
My dear old Mahara. Is he well?
He's dead, my lord. That's why I'm here.
That's bad news. Gurhama found us both.
Gurhama?
I owe you a long explanation.
That's all I want. Why did my father die?

Your father and I were members of the triumvirate
that ruled the Marin-Danim after the civil wars.
What? But that would mean...
...that through your father, you're Marin-Danim. The son of a ruler, in fact.

Well, I never. Until recently, I thought the Marin-Danim were wicked
demons from fairy tales.

Gurhama was the third member. Your father and
I tried to restore our people's original purpose:
to use our technological superiority for discreet intervention,
maintaining peace, order and prosperity on Janatris.

Gurhama pretended to agree, but apparently he had other plans
from the start. He soon took control of the army, and
of research, or what remained of it. In secret, he turned
it towards creating new creatures to serve him. That's how Gurha
came to be.

By the time we found out, it was too late.
We barely managed to escape, taking two important shems used
to activate the most powerful weapons and devices.

We had no choice but to disappear among the other peoples.
Your father stayed in Relov; I settled here in Avaral.
But Gurhama never gave up. Besides his hatred for us,
he desperately needs our shems.
Why are they so important?

If he found all four, he could activate the
weapons systems of the spaceship hidden beneath the
Marin-Danim stronghold, the Fortress.
How so?

The first Marin-Danim stayed aboard the ship, while
the ancestors of the other peoples spread across the
planet. That's why the Marin-Danim preserved the most ancient knowledge.

Eventually, there wasn't enough room aboard, so they built homes around the
ship and on top of it. Over thousands of years,
the whole ship vanished under layers of earth, and the Fortress
rose above it. But the ship is still there.
Did Gurhama find your shem?

Not mine. Fortunately, Gurha isn't very bright. I lost my mind
before Penza's thugs could beat its hiding place out of
me. But I'm worried about your father's shem. How did
he die?

My sister poisoned him. I've already uncovered that. But some man put her
up to it. From the description, he could have been Marin-Danim. She tried
to blame me.

They probably expected your sister to help them find the shem, but
you upset their plans. In that case, it should still be in Relov.

Gooka, you must go home. If you can, find the shem and bring
it back before they get to it.

All right, I'll try. One more question. I found this
in the labyrinth on Glux's island. He said it's
a controller, but it doesn't do anything.
Where did you get that? Was it really in Glux's labyrinth?
Yes.

I didn't believe anything like this still existed
on Jantaris. It's an ancient Terran controller. Only
two were ever brought to Jantaris.
note: Source uses Jantaris, elsewhere Janatris. Variant retained.

english: What is it?

It can do almost anything, but you need the shems.
The more shems you have, the more you
can do with it. With one, for instance,
you can operate most Marin-Danim electronic devices.

With two, you can control all creatures
whose genetic code has been altered. Even Gurha.
What can it do with three shems?

I don't know. No more than two have ever been used
together. I think the controller could help you in your search. I'll
lend you my shem so you can activate it.
Thank you.

I think you now know everything you need. I have plenty
of work waiting for me here in Avaral. Good luck.

I've heard your library has the world's
greatest collection of books about our beloved god Glux.

Of course it does. We have writings by all
our saints. To start at the
beginning, there's Saint Alferos, Ametig, Anorad, Apid, Asanare...
I think that's enough.

We have six thousand eight hundred volumes altogether,
every one about the god Glux.
Which has the most detailed information about him?

I don't know, but several of our
monks have read almost every book here.
They might help you choose. Brothers
Raschi, Bodelain and Demotef live in the
cells at the start of the corridor.
Thank you.

I'm most grateful, Brother, that you
sent me to your learned brethren.
They recommended Saint Ruiciman's Glux: The Established Facts.

They advised you well. It's a very
well-written book, though in recent years our brothers
have seldom consulted it. They prefer other works...

Thank you, but that one will do. If I need any
further information, I'll be sure to ask your advice.

May I ask you something? I come from the distant Bonian
land and seek information about the god Glux. They say the
most learned scholars are here at Orint Monastery. Whom should I ask?

Forgive the interruption, but the librarian told me you're one
of the few who have read the entire library.

I need to learn as much as possible about the
god Glux. Which book would give me the most reliable information?
Brother Raschi sent me to you.
Brother Demotef sent me to you.
Brother Bodelian sent me to you.
Your brothers sent me to you.
I need the most thorough account of the god Glux's life.

Brother Raschi said he'd recommend a book with a

I'm looking for a book with a silver oval on

I'm looking for a book with a silver oval and a

Thank you, then.
Thank you very much.

Naturally, the library has the most information. You'll find it

Ah, the one with a green and purple Glux on the
cover. I can't remember the title. Perhaps one of my
brothers, Rashi or Bodelian, will remember it.

You probably mean the book with its title in gold
lettering. The name escapes me, but my brothers should know something about it.

I can't remember the title, but it's
definitely the one written in brown ink.

The brothers probably mean the
book written on pale green parchment.

Oh! They should have said so sooner. Saint
Ruiciman wrote it. It's called Glux: The Established Facts.

What do you seek, traveller?
I'm looking for the King of Avaral's adviser.

Then you've come to the wrong place. He's at
the castle. In case you don't know it, that's
the big building on the next rock.
What brings you here, traveller?

The King of Avaral sent me here to contemplate the will of
Glux in peace and study his teachings.

A commendable decision. Our establishment is ready to meet
your every need in that regard.
May I come in, then?

Certainly. But it's customary for travellers to bring
a small gift in honour of Glux.
Excuse me? What sort of gift do you mean?

A truly devout traveller wouldn't ask such foolish questions. Search
your sinful conscience. Come back when you've worked it out.
Yes?
I have a gift for the god Glux.
Yes, that is an interesting gift indeed.
May I come in now?
I'd like to let you in, but I can't.
Why not?

Your gift is very nice, but I'm not sure
such a trifle is worthy of our God's attention.

Yes! That's just the gift to please my
God! What greater gift could there be than
something his faithful servant urgently needs? Come in.
Hello! Is anyone there?
Please open up!

Danim-Glux!

Who dares... You must be that Bonian snoop
Penza warned me about.

You are under arrest, for you are an incorrigible heretic. Not only did you
sow distrust of our words in the soul of our most gracious king, but our
lord Glux refused to accept you as a sacrifice.

That can only mean your soul is so burdened with sin that
you cannot be accepted as an offering! You will therefore be executed.
That's not true. I've spoken to Glux. He isn't...

Ha, ha, ha! What blasphemy! You claim to
have spoken to Glux? You are condemned to death!
You'll never get out of here!

What did that overgrown lizard tell you? About this place?
Anything else? No! Our master is Gurha! Gurha the Time-Devourer! He flies

Working notes for an encyclopaedia of Janatris

The Bonians.

Farmers and craftsmen living mainly in the
south, by the rivers Lov, Teko and Rego.

Their state is a league of cities, each
formally independent and led by a
Patriarch elected for life by a body
of sages and judges. The Council
of Bonian Patriarchs elects a leader
for the entire Bonian people. This is
usually the Patriarch of Relov, their
largest and richest city, which may
therefore be regarded as their capital.

The Bonian population is estimated
at 300,000. Their economy is
highly developed, surpassed
only by that of the Bavends.

They keep no standing army and rarely
wage wars of conquest. In the past century
they have often allied with the Bavends
against the Svans, with the Svans against

the Cymiks, and with Chorians against Bavends,
mainly in defence. Otherwise, they seek
peace and brisk trade with their neighbours.

The Bonians are lukewarm in matters of
faith, though most worship the sea god Glux.

The Svans.

A kingdom on the northern sea.

The Svans prize personal prowess
and heroism above all else; war
is their favourite occupation.
Though formidable warriors
individually, their general lack of
discipline and complete absence
of strategic or tactical thinking
prevent their kingdom from
making lasting conquests. Their
campaigns amount chiefly to raids
on the practically helpless Cymiks.

Their total population is around 250,000.
The Svans traditionally neglect economic
matters, which naturally does their
economy little good. They nevertheless
practise some maritime trade, herding
and other forms of agriculture. Most
craftsmanship is devoted to weapons.

The Svans are fanatical worshippers
of the sea god Glux, to whom they
even sacrifice humans. Near their royal
castle, Avaral, stands Orint Monastery,
the chief centre of Glux's worship.

The Cymiks.

Nomads of the barren plains at
the foot of the Western Mountains.

The Cymiks rank lowest by far
in terms of civilisation. Their
lifestyle is extremely primitive.
They spend most of their time
gathering food, yet often go hungry.

Scattered across the plains in individual
families, they are almost defenceless
against raids by neighbouring peoples.
On the other hand, they own nothing,
so no one except the Svans feels
any need to wage war on them.

Recent reports, however,
suggest that the Cymiks are
rising under a tribal chief
who has begun to build a
centralised power based in Taro.

Note: Legend says that the lands now
inhabited by the Cymiks once held the
powerful Xinian civilisation, centred on the
city of Parentis. Neither its history nor the
circumstances of its fall are known. The ruins
of Parentis still stand, and are said to be
inhabited by dreadful spirits and monsters.

The Bavends.

An advanced civilisation on the
eastern slopes of the Vidce Mountains.

The Bavend Republic is essentially
democratic, with an elected senate
led by two or more consuls. The
senate sits in the capital, Wabena.

The Bavends are sworn pacifists.
If forced to fight, they prefer
mercenaries, though these are
superbly led by Bavend generals.

Their population is around one
million. Their advanced civilisation
underpins a thriving economy.
Ingenious canals irrigate land
that was once arid. They are
skilled craftsmen, renowned
for advanced architecture, and
capable seafarers and traders.

The Chorians.

The Chorians inhabit the north-eastern
foothills of the Loba Mountains.

Their society is strictly
matriarchal: men keep house,
while women hunt and fight.

Like the Cymiks, they have no
central authority. Unlike them,
they are warlike, often engaging
in piracy and raids on land.
They form clans and tribes
living in small coastal villages.

Their population is around 120,000. Their
economy is based on raising sheep
and llamas, and is not highly developed.

Their largest city is Xarag, with
its temple to their god, Charia the
Great. They sacrifice humans to him,
chiefly captives taken on pirate raids.

Freshwater crab.

A ten-legged creature half a
metre across. Its greenish flesh is
delicious and can even be eaten raw.

It lives in communities whose members
each have a special role. Warriors
have a sting; shamans and sorcerers
use small doses of its diluted venom
for the psychedelic visions it brings.


Irikan crystals.

Probably the strongest known naturally
occurring corrosive substance. Almost
unobtainable today, their scant deposits
were mined out by the Xinians long ago.
They are probably of meteoritic origin.

Asmat scorpions.

@4

Enormous mountain scorpions, the
most venomous organisms in Parentis.
They are easily controlled with a
special flute, the Asmat stygra.

Their venom attacks the victim's
nervous system, causing
unbearable pain that soon kills.

A single sting can kill up to a hundred people.
An experienced sorcerer, however, can use
the stygra to control the scorpion precisely
enough that its sting does not kill, making
it a tool of extremely unpleasant torture.

Algi.
@1

The largest feline predator on
Janatris. Its hide is virtually
indestructible, making it very hard
to wound. Its sabre-like jaws,
meanwhile, are a deadly threat to
any careless hunter within reach.

In practice, only very powerful poisons
can be used to hunt it. The Algi's hide has
some blood supply, so a mere scratch
with a potent poison such as barut is
enough. Given the toughness of its hide,
a scratch is all one can hope to inflict.

Its durability gives Algi hide many
practical uses, especially when
handling dangerous substances.

Sincha.

@2

One of the most treacherous animals on
Janatris. This mollusc is a virtually indestructible
carnivore. It lurks in rocky crevices, waiting
to crush its victims with hundreds of teeth.

Reliable reports say corrosives can destroy
it, for example a solution of Irikan crystals
or another sufficiently aggressive substance.
note: Source calls sincha a mollusc; dialogue 1320 calls it a crustacean. Retained.

english:
Galha.

A sea lizard about a metre long,
with massive jaws and spines. Its
skin is used for fencing gloves: it is
very supple but protects the hands
even against fairly heavy blows.


Rampol.

A climbing plant found in Bavendia and
among the Chorians. It can be made into
ropes and cords of excellent quality.

Caustic stalactites.

@3

An aggressive plant found in some
underground spaces. Essentially
colonies of single-celled organisms
resembling stalactites, they feed on
airborne microorganisms and dissolve
the rock beneath them. They contain
large quantities of a highly aggressive
molecular acid that acts chiefly on living
tissue. This gives them many practical
uses, but they must be handled with
extreme care and special equipment.
In practice, only gloves made from
Algi hide are relatively obtainable.

Grango.

A lizard of the Western Mountains. It
lives in herds and is rather shy. The
Cymiks favour it as prey, though its
timidity makes it an uncommon catch.


Tree korel.

A small furry animal with vivid purple
fur. It lives in cat trees, feeding
on leaves and occasionally carrion.

Korels are playful and easily
tamed, but sometimes fall into
inexplicable, dangerous moods,
so they are not often kept.

Harila.

A small blue plant that grows on
rocks. It feeds on the blood of
animals injured by its tiny thorns.


Olamina.

A low-growing plant cultivated by
the Chorians. It grows in rocky
soil and bears nuts twice a year.

Asmat stygra.

A ritual musical instrument. Sorcerers
use it to hypnotise people and
control Asmat scorpions. It is
also said to be used in some
particularly vile rites of black magic.

The Asmat stygra is very rare: it
can only be made from the wood of
the krahut tree, which dies unless
regularly watered with chracht blood.


Likanu.

A creature about the size of two palms.
It sits on its hind feet and has blue fur.

Easily tamed and gentle in
nature, it is a common pet.
